newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Reliance up in light India trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Reliance up in light India trade.

text.p: Reliance Industries' global depositary receipts (GDR) rallied further in London on the back of better than expected first half earnings.
"The stock was firm all day, but largely in line with the domestic market," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.53 points at 61.61 points, with the premium over the local market at 11.35 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 18.19 points, 0.58 percent, to 3,130.21.
Reliance GDRs closed up 55 cents at $10.00/$10.75, having been up around 25 cents for most of the day, at the close, and the stock was still at a discount of around six percent to the underlying.

Reliance announced a three percent rise in first half net profit to 6.51 billion rupees from 6.33 billion a year ago, largely because it did not make any provision for the 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax.
Analysts had been expecting a fall in profits because of the provision.
The market is also awaiting a cut in commercial banks reserve requirements as part of a loosening is policy from the Reserve Bank of India.
The central bank is expected to make its move on Saturday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.23 points at 73.03, a premium of 28.23 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 9.48 points to close provisionally at 830.25.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index fell 0.47 points to 89.33, a premium of 2.04 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index closed 18.92 points or 0.29 percent lower at 6,475.
